walkthroughs.body_html:
Independent Investigation (NEA) — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Independent Investigation (NEA) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Independent Investigation (NEA).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What was the Tohoku earthquake magnitude?
What does a 'large scale' map mean?
options: The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
A large-scale map covers a small area in high detail (e.g. 1:25,000 OS map of one town); a small-scale map covers a large area in less detail (e.g. 1:1,000,000 world atlas).
A large-scale map shows a large area.
Large scale means the map is physically big.

mcqs.q: What are the three cells of global atmospheric circulation?
options: The Hadley cell (equator to 30 degrees), Ferrel cell (30 to 60 degrees) and Polar cell (60 degrees to poles) together redistribute heat from equator to poles.
There is one big Hadley cell from the equator to each pole.
Large scale means the map is physically big.
The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.

mcqs.q: Why does oceanic crust subduct beneath continental crust?
options: Oceanic crust subducts because the ocean pushes it down with its weight.
Large scale means the map is physically big.
Oceanic crust is denser (basaltic) than continental crust (granitic), so when they collide the denser oceanic plate sinks into the mantle, forming a trench and volcanic arc.
Continental crust subducts because it is thicker and heavier.
